stimulus.title: Two samples of argon
stimulus.text: The graph shows the distribution of molecular speeds in two samples of argon gas, X and Y, in identical rigid containers. The samples hold the same number of atoms.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which sample is at the higher temperature? Justify your answer using the graph.

rubric.point: Y, because its distribution is shifted to higher speeds (peak farther right, broader), so its average kinetic energy is greater.
accept: Y; higher speeds mean higher average kinetic energy

parts.sample: Sample Y. Its curve peaks at a higher speed and is spread toward faster speeds, so its atoms have a greater average kinetic energy, which means a higher temperature.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Which sample exerts the greater pressure? Explain in terms of collisions of the atoms with the walls.

rubric.point: Y, because its faster atoms collide with the walls more often and with greater force (same n and V).
accept: Y; more frequent and harder collisions

parts.sample: Sample Y. With the same number of atoms in the same volume, its faster atoms hit the walls more often and each collision pushes harder, so the pressure is greater.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A sample of neon (20.18 g/mol) is at the same temperature as sample X. Compare the average kinetic energy of the neon atoms with that of the argon atoms in X, and calculate the ratio of their average speeds, v(Ne) : v(Ar).

rubric.point: States the average kinetic energies are equal because the temperatures are equal.

accept: square root of the mass ratio

parts.sample: Equal: average kinetic energy depends only on temperature. From ½m(Ne)v(Ne)² = ½m(Ar)v(Ar)², v(Ne)/v(Ar) = √(39.95/20.18) = √1.980 = 1.41, so neon atoms move about 1.41 times as fast.
